name: Guliguli
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Retired entry; lists only Dunn & Ross 2007, Lanyon-Orgill 1953 and the ISO change request. No descriptive source of any kind.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2019. Change Request 2019-022: merge Guliguli [gli] into Kazukuru [kzk] (adopted 2020-01-23). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Rationale only (pp. 2-3): Hammarstrom 2015 and Dunn & Ross 2007 (32-item Guliguli list, 94% cognate with Kazukuru), Davis 2003 (no memory of the name). Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Dunn, Michael & Malcolm Ross. 2007. Is Kazukuru really non-Austronesian? Oceanic Linguistics 46(1): 210-231. doi:10.1353/ol.2007.0018 (MPG PuRe open postprint)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 (pp. 216-218) reproduces the 32 Guliguli forms in Table 1 (p. 217) and argues Guliguli and Dororo are transcription variants of Kazukuru, not dialects; Sec. 4.1 Phonology (pp. 218-219) covers only Waterhouse & Ray's Kazukuru graphemes, five vowels, (C)V syllables and r/l. No mention of stress or accent anywhere. Silent.

sources.citation: Davis, Karen. 2003. A grammar of the Hoava language, Western Solomons. Pacific Linguistics 535. Canberra: ANU. (ANU Open Research handle 1885/146158)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology chapter is about Hoava, not Guliguli. On Guliguli only p.15 (PDF p.31): the dialect names Dororo and Guliguli come from Lanyon-Orgill 1953:125, nobody in present-day Kusaghe had heard of them, Lanyon-Orgill does not identify his informant, and guliguli can mean 'masturbate' in Hoava-Kusaghe, so Davis doubts the language existed. Nothing on Guliguli phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. & B. D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kazukuru 'was reported to have two dialects or sublanguages, Doriri and Guliguli (Lanyon-Orgill 1953)'; Guliguli otherwise only a name in the Kazukuru Family diagram (Fig. 1) and the index. No Guliguli data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. The East Papuan Phylum in general. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1 (PL C-38), 783-804.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp. 787-788: Kazukuru Family (Kazukuru, Guliguli, Dororo) 'now extinct', family status doubtful on limited materials. Classification only; silent.

sources.citation: Haudricourt, A. 1953. [Notice of] Journal of Austronesian Studies vol. 1 pt 1. Journal de la Societe des Oceanistes 9: 386 (Persee)
sources.note: Contents notice of the journal issue (editorial, Codrington tribute, Easter Island tablets); does not mention New Georgia or Guliguli. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Waterhouse, J. H. L. & S. H. Ray. 1931. The Kazukuru language of New Georgia. Man 31: 123-126 (DLI scan on archive.org)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kazukuru proper, not Guliguli. Only phonological remark (p.124): sounds written as in Roviana (ng, q, prenasalised b/d). No accent marks, no stress statement. Silent.

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 2011. On the margins of Pacific linguistics: P. A. Lanyon-Orgill. Language & History 54(2): 164-177.
